hlni.insight: A specific illustrative activity can reveal where you need help; it does not determine which degree suits you.
hlni.audienceGap: Students think difficulty with a task indicates they are in the wrong program.
hlni.viewerChange: Replaces 'I'm not good at this' with 'I need to ask about this specific part'.

reelTitle: B.Com vs BBA: Navigating the Choice
objective: Help students shift from anxiety to productive inquiry.
targetAudience: +2 students seeking accessible, supportive guidance, including students worried about marks, confidence, or belonging

shots.name: The Confusion
shots.visual: Close-up of a student looking frustrated while reading a study case on a laptop.
shots.dialogue: Stuck between B.Com and BBA? It’s easy to feel you’ve chosen the wrong path when a task feels hard.

shots.name: The Method
shots.visual: Handwriting in a journal: 'Task: Read case, identify risks. Sticking point: How to quantify 'brand risk'?'
shots.dialogue: Note exactly where you get stuck. It’s not a failure; it’s data for your next conversation.
shots.onscreenText: Task: Read case, identify risks. Sticking point: How to quantify 'brand risk'?

shots.name: The Outcome
shots.visual: Student closing the journal, looking focused and calm.
shots.dialogue: Ask: 'What tools do you use to measure qualitative brand risk?' Use that to learn, not judge yourself.
shots.onscreenText: What tools do you use to measure qualitative brand risk?

creativeSummary.keyCreativeIdea: Transforming the anxiety of a difficult task into a targeted question for inquiry.

selected.title: The Sticking Point Journal
selected.audienceGap: Students feel anxious because they struggle with a random task and assume this means they chose the wrong degree.
selected.hlni: A short illustrative activity can reveal where you need help or what you want to investigate next; it cannot determine which degree suits you.
selected.viewerChange: Replaces 'I'm not good at this' with 'I need to ask about this specific part'.
selected.concept: A student records exactly where they get stuck on a sample task to formulate a better question for a senior.
selected.device: A handwritten log where a student tracks a moment of confusion and turns it into a targeted question.
selected.support: The observation belongs to this activity and participant; it supports a next question rather than a general prediction.
methodSteps: Try or inspect a clearly illustrative task.
Record one point where you needed help and one question you want to investigate.
Turn the observation into a question for a real course brief or course team.
selected.interpretationRule: Use the recorded observation to choose the next question, not to select a degree from one activity.
selected.visibleProof: A person records a specific sticking point and asks a different, more useful question afterward.
selected.payoff: Use the recorded observation to choose the next question, not to select a degree from one activity.
selected.limitations: A brief exercise does not measure aptitude, learning style, long-term interest or academic performance.

demonstration.input: A sample business case study task.
demonstration.visibleInput: Task: Read case, identify risks. Sticking point: How to quantify 'brand risk'?
demonstration.observation: The student identifies a specific gap in their knowledge of risk metrics.
demonstration.nextQuestion: What tools do you use to measure qualitative brand risk?

comparedWith.hlni: A task label alone does not tell you what you must produce, what will be assessed, or what feedback you receive. Ask these as separate questions.
comparedWith.device: Split-screen comparison of two project prompts showing how different grading criteria change the focus of the task.

comparedWith.hlni: A short illustrative activity can reveal where you need help or what you want to investigate next; it cannot determine which degree suits you.
comparedWith.device: A handwritten log where a student tracks a moment of confusion and turns it into a targeted question.

comparedWith.hlni: One unlabeled example does not prove which category or programme contains it. An exclusive claim needs information that actually links the example to that category.
comparedWith.device: A riddle-style presentation showing one element and asking the viewer to 'guess' the degree, followed by the reveal that it's impossible.

conceptSelection.contrast: Trust uses a structural audit of criteria to build verification habits; Connection uses a personal journal to manage anxiety via specific questioning; Discovery uses a logical reveal to expose the fallacy of jumping to conclusions based on partial data.
